messages.subject: different rsfDF and ssDF
parts:
Hello,

I was wondering if it was possible to combine a fecal DNA-based SCR with fully independent telemetry data. We have 48 SCR study sites and 12 additional sites where we collared individuals. I created a rsfDF completely separate from my ssDF but am running into an error (below) when I try to run a model. Is this error due to the different number of sessions between the RSF and SCR?

Error in YYtel[[s]] : subscript out of bounds

Thanks,
John

messages.subject: Re: [oscr] different rsfDF and ssDF
parts:
Hello,

did you perhaps come to any conclusion about this error?

I encountered a similar issue, the error occured while trying to create data2oscr from camera trapping data from 5 temporal sessions (one edf with session_ID column, and 5 tdfs in a list without session_ID column). In each session, there's a different number of traps, but the number of occasions is the same.

Here's the code:

data_slo_nms <- data2oscr(edf=edf_1823_nms,
                            tdf=list(tdf_1, tdf_2, tdf_3, tdf_4, tdf_5),
                            sess.col = 5, # session column in edf
                            id.col = 4, # ID column in edf
                            occ.col = 2, # occasion column in edf
                            trap.col = 1, # trap ID column in edf
                            sex.col = 3, # sex in edf
                            sex.nacode=c("U"), # stating how unknown sex is marked
                            trapcov.names = c("location_type"), # adding info about covariate in tdf
                            tdf.sep ="/", # separator in tdf
                            K=K.nms, # number of occasions
                            ntraps = n.traps.nms # number of traps
)

And the error message:

Error in y3d[xx[obs, "individual"], xx[obs, "trap"], xx[obs, "occasion"]] : subscript out of bounds

Thanks in advance!

Perhaps this still helps someone some day.

messages.author: 527d9b3ec7deff2d
messages.subject: Re: [oscr] different rsfDF and ssDF
parts:
Glad you were able to figure it out.  I've assisted John with some strategies that will hopefully be helpful for making inferences.

In general, oSCR is not designed for John's setup where there are many encounter sessions and telemetry sessions that are distinct from each other, with interest in estimating session-specific parameters.  I think it can be made to work by combining the sessions (instead of 48 separate grids, think of 1 single state space with 48 pockets of encounter surveys) and making some assumptions about shared parameters.
